claim_summary: TSOrchestra combines forecasting-specific ensemble optimization with a fine-tuned LLM judge that revises metric selection, stopping decisions, and explanations from optimization feedback.

claim_evidence.quote: To address this gap, we propose TSOrchestr, which positions LLMs as intelligent judges that evaluate, explain, and strategically coordinate ensembles of specialized forecasting models, thereby combining the numerical precision of time series foundation methods with the interpretive power of language models.

modules.name: Forecasting ensemble optimization and continuation control
modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because candidate weights and continue/accept choices are judged by forecasting performance; changing task family requires replacing the forecast objective, model pool, and validation criterion. GTS would fit temporal dependence alone, but this embeds the forecasting objective; GH would fit task-neutral execution.
rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - forecast objective and validation criterion are embedded
R3_2_GTS:no - temporal semantics are present but the forecasting objective is binding

modules.name: SFT and GRPO adaptation of the ensemble judge
modules.scope_reason: R2 places the parameter updates on the LLM side: SFT and GRPO train the model to make temporal ensemble workflow decisions and grounded explanations, rather than prompting an unchanged model.

evidence.quote: We address these gaps through a two-stage training approach that transforms a general-purpose LLM into a specialized ensembledecider: supervised fine-tuning (SFT) teaches structured decision protocols through expert-annotated trajectories, while reinforcement learning (GRPO) refines these capabilities

modules.name: Synthetic optimization trajectory training data
modules.scope_reason: R2 treats purpose-built examples that train the model as LLM-side contributions; these trajectories teach forecasting workflow decisions and evidence-grounded explanations.

modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the stored optimization history and synthesis concern forecast weights, metrics, and task-specific faithfulness; changing the task changes the evidence and synthesis. R3_2_GTS:no - no independent temporal availability mechanism

modules.scope_reason: R3_1_TSK applies because the validator checks attribution of forecasting performance to temporal components; its criterion changes with the task objective. rubric_path: R3_1_TSK:yes - criterion is causal contribution to forecast performance
R3_2_GTS:no - temporal decomposition alone does not determine its criterion
